review_notes: I read the whole target file and the definition of addDirichletUnit in ParameterShift.lean. I also read its existing simp lemma (sum_addDirichletUnit) and the private duplicate addDirichletUnit_eq_add_single in Average/Deriv.lean. The file has no simp attributes of its own. The only simp-interface problem I found is that addDirichletUnit has no canonical simp lemmas for evaluation or for the b + Pi.single form. This forces repeated by_cases/unfolding proofs. I did not run Lean, so I did not check whether the proposed simp lemmas would loop or conflict. I expect them not to: they are orientation-safe, and the definitional unfolding is replaced rather than competing.

findings.problem: addDirichletUnit is a plain def (Function.update b i (b i + 1)) with no simp lemmas for evaluation (at i, at k ≠ i) and no simp lemma relating it to b + Pi.single i 1. The only simp lemma is sum_addDirichletUnit. So every proof about it unfolds the definition and case-splits on indices: `by_cases hk : k = i <;> simp [addDirichletUnit, hk]` at lines 29 and 98, `simp_all [addDirichletUnit, sub_add_cancel]` at lines 91 and 95, and `show addDirichletUnit b i j = b j by simp [addDirichletUnit, hji]` at line 185. The same equation as h is also proved as a private lemma, addDirichletUnit_eq_add_single, in Average/Deriv.lean. Passing the definition to simp exposes Function.update internals, and simp_all with the definition in the set is fragile.
findings.proposed_change: In ParameterShift.lean, next to sum_addDirichletUnit, add simp lemmas `addDirichletUnit_self : addDirichletUnit b i i = b i + 1`, `addDirichletUnit_of_ne (h : j ≠ i) : addDirichletUnit b i j = b j` (a simp lemma with a side condition), and the non-private `addDirichletUnit_eq_add_single : addDirichletUnit b i = b + Pi.single i 1`. Optionally add `addDirichletUnit_sub_single : addDirichletUnit (b - Pi.single i 1) i = b`. Then drop the private copy in Deriv.lean. Replace h, hi, hj, hij' and the `show` at line 185 by `simp`/`rw` with these lemmas. Do not make addDirichletUnit_eq_add_single a simp lemma without checking against the evaluation lemmas. As a plain lemma it already replaces the `ext`/`by_cases` proofs.
findings.benefit: Shift terms can then be normalized without unfolding the definition. The proofs hi, hj, hij' and h become one-line simp/rw calls. The duplicate private lemma disappears. Downstream files (Deriv.lean, ParameterShift.lean, Associated/Relations.lean) that use `simp [addDirichletUnit, ...]` get a stable interface even if the definition changes.
